summary: A humorous, satirical article about emerging EdTech trends in 2023 classrooms, imagining robot teachers, virtual reality field trips, coding replacing penmanship, 3D printing, gamification, AI-personalized learning and digital libraries. Each trend is illustrated with comic mishaps and invented examples. It closes by joking that the classroom of the future is a playground of boundless imagination.
one_line: A tongue-in-cheek tour of 2023 classroom technology trends, from robot teachers and VR field trips to 3D printing, gamification and AI tutors.
key_facts: Mr. Bolt is a robotic teacher with beaming LEDs who greets students with bleeps and bloops, and remembers Timmy's peanut allergy and Sally's liking for Picasso.
In November 2023, the "EducatorBot 3000" made headlines for managing a classroom for an entire day without locking students in an infinite loop of algebraic functions.
Mrs. Goggles, introduced in 2023, is a virtual reality kit that takes students from the surface of Mars to the inner workings of a cell.
With VR, historians reenact the Battle of Hastings and geography students scale Everest before lunch; glitches can strand students on a digital desert island.
As of December 2023, penmanship is said to have morphed into coding competence, with second-graders debugging homework and learning Python.
Young Jimmy accidentally hacked the school's cafeteria menu, resulting in a surge of chocolate pudding for lunch.
Educators have hailed the 'Syntax Error' as the new 'Spelling Mistake' to be embraced and debugged.
In 3D printing classes, pupils craft with bioplastic; the drama department printed props for its annual play "Romeo and Juliet".
Suzie tried to print a life-size horse for her history project but scaled it wrong and got a miniature pony.
"EduGamification" uses points, badges and levelling up, with students tackling math monsters and defeating the Essay Dragon.
Parents must be convinced that 'Quest for Quantum Physics' is legitimate study time.
AI-driven personalized learning platforms adapt curricula to each student; Pop Quiz Bot predicted Steven's need for extra calculus practice before his first class.
Tablets and techbooks replace the school library, 'book reports' became 'digital narrative experiences', and a holographic librarian keeps reminding students to return e-books on time.
